tools.workflow.list: List the saved workflow scripts in <!-- personal-only:start -->the user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->this Muse's<!-- group-only:end --> workspace. Each entry carries the invocation name, the script's declared workflow name, description, phases, script path, script hash, and last-updated time; a script that cannot be read is listed with an error note instead of failing the whole call. Results are sorted by name and at most limit entries return (default 100, maximum 200). This lists saved scripts only: for this session's runs use workflow.list_runs, and for one script's full source use workflow.view.
tools.workflow.stop: Stop one workflow run by run id. Stopping is terminal: the run's remaining work is cancelled and a stopped run must never be resumed or relaunched; the resumeFromRunId retry path exists only for failed runs. Only runs belonging to this root session can be controlled. To suspend a run you intend to continue, use workflow.pause instead; to stop only one child agent while the run continues, use workflow.stop_agent.
tools.workflow.view: View one saved workspace workflow script by its invocation name. Returns the script source plus its metadata: the script's declared workflow name, description, phases, script path, hash, and last-updated time. Use it to read a script before replacing it with workflow.update or launching it by name with workflow.launch. The call fails when no saved workflow with that name exists; list the available names with workflow.list.
tools.workflow.pause: Pause one workflow run by run id. Only a queued or running run changes state: pausing an already paused run is a no-op, and a terminal (succeeded, failed, stopped, or cancelled) run cannot be paused. The run keeps its progress and can continue later with workflow.resume. Only runs belonging to this root session can be controlled. To end a run permanently use workflow.stop instead.
tools.workflow.create: Create a new saved workflow script in <!-- personal-only:start -->the user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->this Muse's<!-- group-only:end --> workspace. Saved workflows live in the workspace's saved-workflows directory and can be launched by name later with workflow.launch or workflow.launch_async. The call fails if a saved workflow with that name already exists; replace an existing one with workflow.update instead. Creating a workflow only stores the script and never runs it. Setting up a reusable workflow usually also needs workflow.launch or workflow.list.
tools.workflow.delete: Delete one saved workflow script by its invocation name from the workspace's saved-workflows directory. The response echoes the deleted definition. Deleting a saved script never touches runs: past runs stay inspectable with workflow.view_run, and a running workflow keeps executing its own script snapshot (stop it with workflow.stop). The call fails when no saved workflow with that name exists.
tools.workflow.launch:
Launch a VM-local JavaScript workflow and wait for it to resolve. The result carries the run id, final status, and the workflow's curated final return, so use this when the caller should block on the outcome; use workflow.launch_async to return immediately instead.
Provide exactly one script source: scriptPath (a workspace-contained JavaScript file, highest precedence), script (inline source), or name (a saved workspace workflow). scriptPath takes precedence over script, and script takes precedence over name. Pass structured input as the args object. A workflow session usually also needs siblings such as workflow.list, workflow.view_run, or workflow.stop.
tools.workflow.resume: Resume one paused workflow run by run id. Resuming continues the same run in place; when the run was launched synchronously, this call waits for the resumed run to resolve and returns its outcome. Only a paused run that can continue without new <!-- personal-only:start -->user input<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->input from a member<!-- group-only:end --> qualifies. For a terminal failed run caused by a retryable provider, runtime, or other transient execution error, do not resume: launch the same workflow again with the same args and resumeFromRunId set to the failed run id (workflow.launch or workflow.launch_async). A stopped or cancelled run is terminal and must never be resumed or relaunched, and neither recovery path may be used to bypass missing input, access, approval, policy, syntax, validation, or other deterministic failures. Only runs belonging to this root session can be controlled.
tools.workflow.update: Replace the script of an existing saved workspace workflow. The call fails if no saved workflow with that name exists; create a new one with workflow.create instead. The new script affects only future launches by name: runs that already started keep the script snapshot they launched with. Read the current source first with workflow.view.
tools.workflow.save_run: Save a workflow run's script snapshot as a saved workspace workflow, so the exact script that ran can be launched again by name later with workflow.launch or workflow.launch_async. The optional name picks the saved workflow name; when omitted, the run's own workflow name is used. Saving overwrites an existing saved workflow with the same name. The script is taken from the run's verified snapshot, not from whatever file the run was originally launched from. Only runs belonging to this root session can be controlled.
tools.workflow.view_run: View one workflow run by run id: its status, phase progress, child agent calls with their call ids, timing, and any final result or error. Only runs belonging to this root session are visible. Use it to follow a run started with workflow.launch_async, to pick the callId that workflow.stop_agent needs, or to confirm whether a run is paused, failed, or terminal before resuming it with workflow.resume or retrying it through a new launch with resumeFromRunId. Find run ids with workflow.list_runs.
tools.workflow.list_runs: List the workflow runs launched from this root session, with each run's id, workflow name, status, and timing. Use it to find the run id that workflow.view_run and the run control tools (workflow.pause, workflow.resume, workflow.stop, workflow.stop_agent, workflow.save_run) require. At most limit rows return. For the saved scripts rather than runs, use workflow.list.
tools.workflow.stop_agent: Stop one child agent call inside a workflow run without stopping the run. Requires the run id and the callId of the child agent call; workflow.view_run lists the run's child calls and their call ids. The run itself keeps going; use workflow.stop to end the whole run. Only runs belonging to this root session can be controlled.
tools.workflow.launch_async:
Launch a VM-local JavaScript workflow asynchronously and return immediately with the run id while the workflow keeps executing in the background. Follow progress with workflow.view_run and control the run with workflow.pause or workflow.stop; use workflow.launch when the caller should wait for the result instead.
Provide exactly one script source: scriptPath (a workspace-contained JavaScript file, highest precedence), script (inline source), or name (a saved workspace workflow). scriptPath takes precedence over script, and script takes precedence over name. Pass structured input as the args object. An async launch usually also needs workflow.view_run and workflow.list_runs to follow the run.

fields.list.limit: Optional maximum saved workflows to return. Defaults to 100; values are clamped to at most 200.
fields.stop.runId: Workflow run id, as returned by a launch or listed by workflow.list_runs. Stopping is terminal; a stopped run can never be resumed or relaunched.
fields.view.name: Saved workspace workflow invocation name to view.
fields.pause.runId: Workflow run id, as returned by a launch or listed by workflow.list_runs. Only a queued or running run changes state.
fields.create.name: Invocation name for the new saved workflow. Fails if a saved workflow with this name already exists.
fields.create.script: Complete JavaScript workflow source to save, authored per the contract in this tool's description.
fields.delete.name: Saved workspace workflow invocation name to delete.
fields.resume.runId: Workflow run id, as returned by a launch or listed by workflow.list_runs. The run must be paused; a synchronous run's resume waits for it to resolve.
fields.update.name: Invocation name of the existing saved workflow to replace. Fails if no saved workflow with this name exists.
fields.update.script: Complete replacement JavaScript workflow source, authored per the contract in this tool's description.
fields.runId: Workflow run id, as returned by a launch or listed by workflow.list_runs.
fields.save_run.name: Optional saved workflow name for the snapshot. Defaults to the run's own workflow name; an existing saved workflow with the same name is overwritten.
fields.stop_agent.callId: Workflow child agent call id to stop, as listed in workflow.view_run details.
fields.launch.scriptPath: Workspace-local or absolute workspace-contained JavaScript workflow file path to launch. Takes precedence over script and name.
fields.launch.script: Inline self-contained JavaScript workflow source, authored per the contract in this tool's description. Used when scriptPath is absent; takes precedence over name.
fields.launch.name: Saved workspace workflow invocation name to launch. Used when scriptPath and script are absent.
fields.launch.args: Structured input exposed verbatim to the launched workflow as the global `args`. Pass arrays and objects as JSON values, not as JSON-encoded strings. The script reads fields directly from `args`; it must not redeclare `args`.
fields.launch.resumeFromRunId: Run id of a terminal failed run to retry from. The source run must use the same root session, workspace, and workflow name; completed stable-key child results can be reused. Use workflow.resume instead when the existing run is paused.
